scenes.title: Towser
scenes.narration: February the twenty-third, 1847. Today. I shot our dog, Towser. I wrote it down in my little book, the way I write everything down. Outside, the snow has buried our cabin to the roof. My name is Patrick Breen. Eighty-one of us are trapped in these mountains. And my family, all nine of us will walk out alive. This is how.

scenes.title: Ten months earlier
scenes.narration: Ten months earlier. Spring, 1846. We leave our farm in Iowa with seven children, our wagons and a herd of cattle. Thousands of families are heading west this year, to Oregon and California. I am fifty-one years old, an Irishman who has already crossed one ocean. What is one more continent?

scenes.title: My family
scenes.narration: My wife, Peggy. Forty years old, and the strongest person I have ever known. Our boys: John, Edward, Patrick, Simon, James and little Peter. And Isabella, not even a year old, in her mother's arms. Every night on the trail, we pray the rosary together. I did not know yet how much we would need it.

scenes.title: The shortcut
scenes.narration: In July, at Fort Bridger, we hear about a new route. A man named Lansford Hastings has written a book about it: a shortcut, he says, that will save hundreds of miles. Our group decides to take it. The old trail hands shake their heads. But the rest of us we just want to reach California before the snow.

scenes.title: No road
scenes.narration: The shortcut is a lie. In the Wasatch Mountains there is no road at all. For weeks, our men cut one themselves, with axes, through forest and boulders. Some days we move one mile. Then comes the salt desert: eighty miles of white crust, with no water and no grass. Our oxen fall and do not get up.

scenes.title: Driven out
scenes.narration: By October we are a month behind, worn out, and angry. In a quarrel by the Humboldt River, a man named James Reed kills another man, John Snyder. The company drives Reed out, ahead of us, into the wilderness. His wife and four children stay behind with us. Nobody knows yet that Reed will come back.

scenes.title: The lake
scenes.narration: On the last day of October, we reach a lake below the pass, the final wall of mountains before California. We can see the gap at the top. One more climb, and we are through. That night it starts to snow.

scenes.title: Turned back
scenes.narration: We try. Men, women, children, oxen, all pushing up toward the pass. The snow is so deep we cannot even find the road. Three miles from the summit, we turn back. Later I write it in my book: 'The snow so deep we were unable to find the road.'

scenes.title: Trapped
scenes.narration: Then the real storm comes. For eight days it snows, and snows, and does not stop. The pass is closed. Eighty-one of us are trapped on the wrong side of the mountains. Most of us here at the lake the Donner families a few miles away, at Alder Creek.

scenes.title: The cabin
scenes.narration: We are lucky in one thing. By the lake stands an old log cabin, built two years before by other emigrants. We take it. Other families build cabins nearby. Ours has a dirt floor, a stone fireplace, and a roof patched with hides and branches. Nine of us in one small room.

scenes.title: Peggy's rule
scenes.narration: Peggy makes the first rule. Every piece of meat is counted. Every handful of flour. She hides some away, even from me. 'We eat little, so we can eat long,' she says. In November, other cabins eat well. By January they have nothing.

scenes.title: The snow takes the cattle
scenes.narration: We kill our oxen and cows and freeze the meat in the snow. The snow is our icebox. But the snow also steals from us. In the storms, some of the cattle wander off and are buried. Under ten feet of white, nobody can find them again.

scenes.title: The diary
scenes.narration: I keep my diary every day. The weather, the wind, who is sick. 'Snow about three feet deep.' Then, 'six feet.' Then, 'eight feet on the level.' And in January: 'must be thirteen feet deep.' We dig steps up from our door just to reach the daylight.

scenes.title: The Forlorn Hope
scenes.narration: In December, seventeen of the strongest decide to cross the mountains on homemade snowshoes, to bring help. They call themselves the Forlorn Hope. They take food for six days. The journey will take them thirty-three. Only seven of them will reach the valley.

scenes.title: Christmas
scenes.narration: Christmas Day. I write: 'Began to snow yesterday snowed all night, and snows yet rapidly. Great difficulty in getting wood.' Peggy has saved a little something for the children. We pray. And outside, the wind screams down off the mountains.

scenes.title: Hides
scenes.narration: By January, the meat is gone. So we eat the hides. Peggy cuts the ox hides into strips, singes off the hair, and boils them for hours, until they turn into a thick, grey glue. It tastes of nothing. I write: 'Hides are the only article we depend on. May God send us help.'

scenes.narration: Then the bones. We boil them again and again, and when they give nothing more, we burn them and eat them like crackers. The children catch mice. We chew bark, and twigs, and the leather of old shoes. Nothing is wasted. Nothing.

scenes.title: The dying
scenes.narration: Others are not so lucky. In the cabins around us, people begin to die. First the weakest: the old, the babies and the young men who worked the hardest. The ground is frozen hard as iron, so the dead are laid to rest in the snow.

scenes.title: Two of our boys
scenes.narration: Twenty-three people leave with them, mostly children and mothers. Two of our boys go too, Edward and Simon. Peggy holds them for a long time. The rest of us stay, and wait for the next rescue. We still have hides. Others have nothing at all.

scenes.title: Our dog
scenes.narration: Five days later, I do the thing I have been putting off. 'Shot Towser today,' I write, 'and dressed his flesh.' Our dog. The children loved him. That same morning, a neighbour comes to borrow meat. They think I have meat to spare. I know to the contrary.

scenes.title: What I will not say
scenes.narration: By now, there is talk in the camp that I will not repeat to you. When the living have nothing left some of them turn to the dead. In my diary, I write only what I hear. And I pray it never comes to that in our cabin.

scenes.title: Reed comes back
scenes.narration: On the first of March, ten more men arrive. And leading them is James Reed. The man we drove out in October. He crossed the mountains and now he has come back for his family. I write my last line: 'We are to start in two or three days.'

scenes.title: Starved Camp
scenes.narration: We leave the lake with Reed's party, seventeen of us. Two days out, a blizzard hits. Reed's men are starving too. They push ahead to bring back food and leave us behind, my family and a few others, around one fire in the snow. Later, people will call this place Starved Camp.

scenes.title: Peggy's fire
scenes.narration: And here, Peggy saves us all. The heat of our fire melts the snow beneath it, and it sinks deeper and deeper into a pit. She keeps it burning. She feeds it every log we have, holds the baby against her chest, and does not sleep. What else happened at that camp. I leave between me and God.

scenes.title: John Stark
scenes.narration: After about a week, men come up through the snow: the third rescue. One of them, a big man named John Stark, refuses to leave anyone behind. He carries the little ones on his back, two at a time, all the way down the mountain.

scenes.title: How we survived
scenes.narration: So how did my family survive, when so many did not? Peggy rationed from the very first day. We stayed together. We ate every hide, every bone. We kept a fire and a reason to live. And we had luck. A lot of luck. And good men who came back for us.

scenes.title: What came after
scenes.narration: Of the eighty-seven people who took that shortcut, thirty-nine died. Forty-eight lived. Ours was one of only two families that came out complete. We settled in San Juan Bautista, in California, and ran an inn for travellers. And our baby, Isabella, lived to be nearly ninety: the very last survivor of us all. If you've stayed with me this far. scenes.title: What comes next
scenes.narration: A hundred and thirty-seven years before us, in France, the coldest winter in five hundred years freezes the rivers, the wine in the barrels and even the sea along the coast. In a small village, a baker has to keep his family alive. How did he do it? That story is next. And here the fire is still burning.
